The *Paṭhamapatibbatāvimānavatthu* (Vv 11) is a verse text in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. In the narrative, a female deva explains the karmic rewards that arose from her past deeds as a human being, detailing the spiritual benefits of staying faithful to one's spouse and remaining honest [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan are cataloged for the discourse on SuttaCentral, and automated analysis via DharmaNexus similarly identifies no cross-language alignments meeting the score threshold [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus registers 195 text-reuse passages across 31 texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest sharing partner is its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which matches 75 passages, including a near-continuous span covering §1.1–8.4 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares substantial formulaic verses with other mansion accounts within the *Vimānavatthu*, most closely with its immediate sequel, the *Dutiyapatibbatāvimānavatthu* (Vv 12, particularly §2.1–5.1), as well as *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Sunikkhittavimānavatthu* (Vv 85), and *Paṭhamanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 6) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral indexes five translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
